title: Conditional normalized projective-line unit and counit on full subcategories
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] with pulled-back coefficients [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use ordinary unbounded internal-module derived categories $D(Z)$, with [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $Y$ be a scheme, $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$, $W=P\times_Y P$, $q,p_1,p_2,\Delta$ as in [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Assume $\Delta$ is closed, its complementary open $j$ is quasi-compact, and the coefficient inverse images along $\Delta,j$ are exact. Fix modules $L_Z$, a diagonal coefficient diagram with class $\delta$ and trace $\tau$ [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-category], and an isomorphism $e:p_2^*(L_P[2])\simeq L_W[2]$. Use the fixed canonical section, tensor, twist and projection maps of [def-sfb-projective-diagonal-composition], [def-sfb-internal-diagonal-tensor-comparison], [def-sfb-tate-twisted-projection-comparison] and the ambient component formulas of [def-sfb-projective-ambient-unit-counit-composites]. Put $T_Z(A)=(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}L_Z)[2]$. Let $\mathcal C_P\subseteq D(P)$ and $\mathcal C_Y\subseteq D(Y)$ be full replete triangulated subcategories. Assume $F=Rq_*$ and $G=T_Pq^*$ restrict to exact functors $\mathcal C_P\to\mathcal C_Y$ and $\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_P$. Assume the fixed exchange and twisted projection are invertible for every $M\in\mathcal C_P$ [def-sfb-rational-p1-unit-inversion-condition], and the fixed left projection is invertible for every $K\in\mathcal C_Y$ [def-sfb-rational-p1-counit-inversion-condition]. Then the canonical diagonal tensor map is a natural isomorphism on all $D(P)$ and $Rp_{2*}R\Delta_*\simeq1$. There is a unique pair of natural transformations $\eta:1\to GF$, $\varepsilon:FG\to1$ on these full subcategories whose underlying components are respectively the fixed ambient diagonal-insertion and trace-contraction formulas. Uniqueness refers to these formulas (heterogeneous equality after the prescribed identifications), not to arbitrary candidate adjunction maps. Both are natural transformations between the specified exact functors; triangle identities are not asserted.

source.note:
Construction material retained from the earlier split. The following proof-in-words was previously attached to this node. It is preserved here verbatim as source material for the worker who will prove the corresponding Lean declaration; this stage-1 node intentionally has no proof steps.

Former proof step 1:
Open and closed restrictions detect isomorphisms even on unbounded complexes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with $X=W$, $i=\Delta$ and ring sheaf $\Lambda_W$. It supplies exact $\Delta_*,j_!$, the identities $\Delta^*\Delta_*\simeq1$, $j^*\Delta_*=0$, and the module sequence $0\to j_!j^*F\to F\to\Delta_*\Delta^*F\to0$. The two inverse images are exact by hypothesis. Thus they act on cohomology sheaves. If $\Delta^*C=j^*C=0$ for an arbitrary complex $C$, then the exact sequence applied to each $H^nC$ has zero outer terms, hence $H^nC=0$ for every integer $n$. Applying this observation to the cone of a morphism proves joint conservativity. Exact sheaf functors induce triangulated functors by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]; [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] also identifies the exact closed pushforward with $R\Delta_*$. No assertion about geometric stalks detecting all pro-etale sheaves is needed.

Former proof step 2:
Diagonal tensor identification, with its actual map. Put $A_M=p_1^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Delta_*\Lambda_P$. The tensor-pullback isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], the pullback composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], and the identities $p_1\Delta=1$ and $\Delta^*\Delta_*\Lambda_P=\Lambda_P$, identify $\Delta^*A_M$ with $M\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Lambda_P=M$. The same tensor-pullback isomorphism gives $j^*A_M=0$ because $j^*\Delta_*\Lambda_P=0$. Use the derived pullback/direct-image adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] to form its unit $a_M:A_M\to\Delta_*\Delta^*A_M=\Delta_*M$. After $\Delta^*$ it is an isomorphism: the triangle identity composes it with the invertible closed counit to give $1$. After $j^*$ it is the map $0\to0$. The identities and closed counit here are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], termwise on complexes as in the preceding step. Joint conservativity from the preceding support argument makes $a_M$ an isomorphism. Define the isomorphism in clause (1) to be $a_M^{-1}$. It is natural in $M$, since $a$ is an adjunction unit followed by natural tensor and pullback identifications. This is the actual fixed diagonal tensor map: under the adjunction hom-equivalence, the left-factor projection followed by the section and unitor of [def-sfb-internal-diagonal-tensor-comparison] has transpose the same canonical identification $\Delta^*A_M\to M$. The unit followed by this identification has that transpose too, by the adjunction triangle identity. Injectivity of the hom-equivalence identifies the two maps; thus the inverse just proved is the prescribed inverse, not an arbitrary support isomorphism.

Former proof step 3:
The initial identification in the unit. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to $P\xrightarrow{\Delta}W\xrightarrow{p_2}P$, with the pulled-back coefficient rings. Since $p_2\Delta=1_P$, it gives $Rp_{2*}R\Delta_*\simeq R(1_P)_*=1$. Here $R\Delta_*=\Delta_*$ by exactness from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] and the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. This is a natural identification for every unbounded $M$. Use its inverse to write $M\simeq Rp_{2*}\Delta_*M$, followed by $Rp_{2*}(a_M^{-1})$.

The fixed left projection has source $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rq_*L_P[2]$ and target $Rq_*(q^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L_P[2])$. Apply $Rq_*$ to inverse tensor-shift, then its assumed inverse, then $1_K\otimes\tau$, the coefficient-unit identification and the right unitor. Former proof step 6:
For $u:M\to M'$, bifunctoriality gives $(p_1^*u\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes\delta)=(1\otimes\delta)\circ(p_1^*u\otimes1)$ with the respective sources and targets. Compose this square with naturality of the section, diagonal tensor, exchange and twisted projection maps; invert the last two naturality squares by composing with their inverses. This proves $GF(u)\eta_M=\eta_{M'}u$. Tensor-shift naturality is exactly [lem-sfb-rational-p1-tensor-shift-naturality]. For $v:K\to K'$, tensor bifunctoriality gives $(v\otimes1)(1\otimes\tau)=(1\otimes\tau)(v\otimes1)$. Compose with inverse tensor-shift, inverse left-projection naturality [lem-sfb-rational-p1-left-projection-naturality], and unitor naturality. This proves $v\varepsilon_K=\varepsilon_{K'}FG(v)$. The projection and tensor structures are exact and shift-compatible by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. The assumed exactness of restricted $F,G$ and exactness of [2] therefore give precisely natural transformations between exact functors.

Former proof step 7:
The component formulas and the two proved naturality equations define both natural transformations on the full subcategories. Work first with abstract coefficient, diagram, predicates and the specified preservation and inversion witnesses; specialize only after constructing these transformations, so no choice of a different tensor or cached inversion predicate occurs. For any other normalized pair, heterogeneous equality to each same fixed ambient component gives heterogeneous equality of the two components by symmetry and transitivity. Their types now agree, hence the components are equal. Morphisms in a full subcategory are the ambient morphisms, so componentwise equality gives equality of each natural transformation and then of the pair. This proves existence and uniqueness without a kernel expansion of the concrete tensor data, and without assuming triangle identities.
